title: extractous output, schema version 1
description: Each line written by `extractous --format json|pages|elements` is one of these records.

path.description: The input as given; `-` for standard input.

size.description: Size of the input in bytes.

embedded_path.description: With --embedded separate: the path of an embedded document inside the input, such as `inbox.mbox/msg-1.eml/report.docx`.

text.description: Extracted text, or XHTML, in `--format json`. Absent when the input could not be opened, and in the closing record of `pages` and `elements`, whose text is in the preceding records.

message.description: The error with its full Java cause chain.

location.description: Where in the input the failure happened, such as `embedded document`, when known.

metadata.description: Normalised metadata, present with --metadata. Fields that are unknown are omitted.

decrypted.description: Present when the document needed a password and one of the given passwords opened it.

ocr.description: How each image or page OCR read was read: the model, the script detection found, and what was done to make the image readable first. An embedded image's report is in its own record.

page.description: The page of a PDF or multi-page image, absent for a single image.

language.description: The tesseract model read with, such as eng, ara or script/Latin.

script.description: The script orientation and script detection found, without --ocr-lang.

exif_orientation.description: The EXIF orientation the image was turned upright by.

prepared.description: Whether the image could be decoded to prepare it; one that could not went to tesseract as it was.

flattened.description: Whether a page photographed at an angle was found and mapped back to a rectangle.

inverted.description: Whether light text on a dark ground was inverted to dark text on a light one.

turned_degrees.description: The clockwise turn orientation detection found and applied.

deskewed_degrees.description: The skew of the text lines that was corrected.

scale.description: The factor the image was resized by before reading: above 1 to enlarge text too small to read, below 1 to reduce large text, which reads as well and faster.

thresholded.description: Whether the image was thresholded for uneven lighting.

rejected_text_layers.description: PDF pages whose text layer was garbage, or read worse than OCR, and was replaced by OCR text under --ocr auto, with the signal that rejected it.

raw_metadata.description: Tika's metadata keys and values, present with --raw-metadata.

duplicate_of.description: With --embedded separate: the embedded path of the first document in this input with the same content, which was extracted instead.

document.description: One per input: the whole result in `--format json`, or the closing record after the pages or elements of `--format pages` and `--format elements`.

page.description: One page of the text (a PDF page, a slide), or the whole text when the format has no pages.
1-based page number; absent for text outside any page.

header.description: The running header taken out of this page's text: a first line that recurs on most pages.

footer.description: The running footer taken out of this page's text, such as a page number: a last line that recurs on most pages.

artifacts.description: The text the document marks as furniture of this page rather than content, such as a tagged PDF's running headers, footers and page numbers, taken out of this page's text.

element.description: One heading, paragraph, list item or table, or text outside any of them, in reading order.

text.description: For tables, cells are separated by tabs and rows by newlines.

date.description: RFC 3339. `utc` when the source gave an offset, `unknown_offset` when it did not; never assumed local.

detected_language.description: The language of the text, detected from the text itself (as opposed to `metadata.language`, which the document declares). Detected from the first 64 KiB of a document's text, and from each page's own text.

script.description: The Unicode script most of the letters are written in, such as `Latin`, `Arabic` or `Han`.

reliable.description: Whether the detection is confident enough to act on, such as to pick a search analyzer.
